The seed query's 'NKBM/OTP' framing must be resolved to a single current entity.

brief: Slovenia's private-bank disclosure landscape is concentrated and post-consolidation: after the 2024 merger of Nova KBM and SKB into OTP banka d.d., the demand-side view of regulation rests on roughly seven institutions — NLB (the only listed issuer, and therefore the only one with a low-latency statutory channel via SEOnet), OTP banka, Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, Addiko, Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica, plus UniCredit and Sparkasse. Every one of them publishes CRR Part Eight 'razkritja' and annual reports in Slovenian, but almost none offer a feed: monitoring means scheduled HTML diffing of 'obvestila za stranke' and 'letna poročila in razkritja' index pages plus PDF harvesting, complicated by OTP's opaque numeric download IDs, NLB's cross-host redirect to nlbgroup.com, and Delavska hranilnica's two parallel domains. The richest early-warning signal is not the Pillar 3 PDF but the two-months-ahead customer notice of changed splošni pogoji and ceniki, which is where deadlines such as the 9 Oct 2025 Instant Payments Regulation become concretely visible; DORA, by contrast, has no dedicated bank-level channel and must be mined from annual-report risk sections. The Banka Slovenije register subjektov nadzora should anchor the crawl list so entity mergers and licence changes do not silently break coverage.
